research_rationale: Executive Order 11990 of May 24, 1977 (42 FR 26961; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11990.txt, read in full) is the wetlands protection order: section 1 directs each agency to minimize destruction of wetlands in land management, construction and land-use activities (excluding permits to private parties on non-Federal property); section 2 requires findings before new construction in wetlands and early public review; section 3 requires budget requests to state accord with the order; section 4 governs disposal of Federally owned wetlands; section 5 lists factors; section 6 requires agency procedures; section 7 defines terms; section 8 states transitional exclusions and an October 1, 1977 implementation date; section 9 excludes emergency work; section 10 allows applicants to assume responsibilities. The only amendment found is Executive Order 12608 section 28 (September 9, 1987), which struck 'and the Water Resources Council' from section 6. The U.S. Code note prints the order as amended and a July 10, 2026 Federal Register proposed rule of the Department of Housing and Urban Development cites it as in force. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: The order sets continuing duties and definitions for agencies. The only dated provisions are in section 8 (a 1977 cut-off for projects excluded and an October 1, 1977 implementation date), which are transitional and were not used up in a way that ends any command. Nothing was transferred or accrued outside the order.
earlier_end_check: Own terms: no section has an until-date or expiry; the October 1, 1977 date in section 8 is an implementation deadline and an exclusion cut-off, not an end. No earlier revocation or supersession appears in the Office of the Federal Register note, the printed U.S. Code note, or the three bounded searches.
scope_check: Scope: the eighteen clauses of the dossier inventory cover the preamble-free text from section 1 through section 10 and are confirmed against the held text. The one amendment, Executive Order 12608 section 28, touches section 6 only.
independent_command_check: Independent commands: sections 1 to 5 state separate agency commands, section 6 the procedure duty, section 7 definitions, sections 8 to 10 exclusions and an applicant provision; each is recorded as its own clause and none depends on another ending.
savings_check: Savings: the order establishes continuing agency duties; no performance, report or transfer is outstanding or used up beyond the 1977 implementation date, which does not end any command.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12146 of July 18, 1979 (44 FR 42657; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12146.txt, read in full) establishes the Federal Legal Council (section 1-1), states its functions (1-2), requires a litigation notice system (1-3), directs legal disputes between Executive agencies to the Attorney General (1-4), encourages public availability of legal opinions (1-5), provides for automated legal research and information systems (1-6) and sets agency responsibilities (1-7). Executive Order 12608 section 15 (1987) updated the name of the Department of Health and Human Services and Executive Order 13286 section 53 (2003) raised the member limit from 15 to 16 and added the Department of Homeland Security to the initial list. The two-year initial term of section 1-103 ended the initial-membership roster in 1981. The dossier chain lists Executive Order 12977 for this order but the provision it quotes is the Executive Order 13286 section 53 amendment (the held text of Executive Order 12977 does not mention Executive Order 12146), so it is not treated as an amendment. The order is operative on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: The initial roster ended with the initial term in 1981; the standing provisions of the order are continuing commands. Nothing was transferred or accrued.
earlier_end_check: Own terms: the only time-limited provision is the initial two-year term in section 1-103 (and the one-year report date in section 1-701, a deadline that does not end the order). No earlier revocation or supersession appears in the Office of the Federal Register note or the bounded searches.
scope_check: Scope: the 39 clauses of the dossier inventory cover sections 1-101 to 1-702 including the lettered lists and are confirmed against the held text; the combined printed entry of items (f) and (g) is one clause. Executive Order 13286 section 53 changed section 1-101 and 1-102 only; Executive Order 12608 section 15 changed the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare name.
independent_command_check: Independent commands: the establishment, the roster, the functions of the Council, the litigation notice system, the dispute-submission rule, the legal-opinion encouragement, the research systems and the agency duties are separate commands, each decided on its own.
savings_check: Savings: no performance, report or transfer is outstanding beyond the 1980 and 1981 dates already discussed.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12432 of July 14, 1983 (48 FR 32551; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12432.txt, read in full) has two sections. Section 1 requires Federal agencies with substantial procurement or grantmaking authority to develop minority business enterprise development plans, submit them annually to the Cabinet Council on Commerce and Trade, follow uniform guidelines set by the Secretary of Commerce and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration, report annually, and requires the Secretary of Commerce to report annually to the President. Section 2 requires agencies to establish minority business development programs, to encourage grant recipients to achieve minority business participation, and to give the Cabinet Council information on progress. The text states no date, duration, condition or expiry. The packet inventory missed the end of paragraph 2(c) and paragraph 2(d), which print after the Federal Register page break, so the inventory is corrected to ten clauses (inventory overrides). No amendment, revocation or supersession of the order appears in the held Federal Register texts of later orders (a search of the held texts for citations of this order by number found only regulations and rules that implement or cite it), in the Office of the Federal Register catalog (no disposition note), or in the three bounded searches. The eCFR (48 CFR 1426.7100 and 1426.7102-1; 24 CFR 5.105) and the U.S. Code note under 15 U.S.C. 631 treat the order as continuing. The held sources do not show what body now stands in the place of the Cabinet Council on Commerce and Trade, and none says that an end of the Council ended any command of the order; that open point is disclosed in the clauses that name the Council. All ten clauses are operative on 2026-10-14. Standing note on sources: the original is held as a machine text layer of the official Federal Register page; check the page before relying on quotations.

scope_check: Scope: the packet's inventory of nine clauses was incomplete (the end of paragraph 2(c) and all of paragraph 2(d) print after the page break); the corrected inventory of ten clauses is confirmed against the full held text. No partial amendment or revocation was found.
